title: EIF project-instance configuration (.eif/config.yaml) - user/project-owned
description: Mirrors .eif/config.yaml.example - keep both in sync. Validated by scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --config. This file holds DESIRED, user-owned settings only - it is written once by eif_init and never overwritten by a routine upgrade. EIF-managed provenance (exact framework ref, bundle manifest, generated adapter entrypoint) lives in the separate, fully-regenerated framework-lock.schema.json / .eif/framework.lock.yaml - see docs/architecture/instance-contract.md for why the two are split.

schema_version.description: This config file's own schema version.

framework.description: Optional DESIRED framework release line - not provenance. Which framework commit actually generated this instance is recorded in .eif/framework.lock.yaml, not here.

adapter.description: User's declared adapter choice. `name` is deliberately NOT an enum here - the registry (scripts/eif_adapters.py) is the single source of truth for valid names, enforced by eif_init.py's argparse choices and cross-checked at runtime by eif_verify_runtime.py; duplicating the list in this schema would let the two drift silently. The generated entrypoint file and verified-version evidence are managed provenance - see .eif/framework.lock.yaml.

options.description: Optional, per-adapter settings this adapter's own registry entry (scripts/eif_adapters.py) declares - e.g. Codex's project_doc_fallback_filenames/project_doc_max_bytes. Absent, or an absent key within it, means the adapter's own documented default applies. Hand-edited by the project (not generated by eif_init.py), same as the rest of this user-owned file - read fresh on every upgrade.

codex.description: Mirrors Codex's own ~/.codex/config.toml keys of the same name - re-verified 2026-07-18 directly against Codex's own Rust source (pinned commit 3a067484584861606ad842de5bc4ac735a865ddf on github.com/openai/codex: codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs, codex-rs/config/src/project_root_markers.rs, codex-rs/core/config.schema.json), not from a paraphrased secondary doc page as the first pass was. EIF has no authless way to read config.toml's actual live values (no --json effective-config command exposes them as of codex-cli 0.144.5 - `codex doctor --json` was checked and does not) - these are the project's own asserted values, used only to compute EIF's own active-entrypoint resolution and size-budget checks. They do not change Codex's real configuration; keep them in sync with ~/.codex/config.toml by hand if it changes.

project_doc_fallback_filenames.description: Extra project-doc filenames Codex has been configured to also treat as an instructions file, checked (in the order given, de-duplicated, empty entries skipped) after AGENTS.override.md/AGENTS.md at the instance root. Codex's own documented default (and JSON-schema-declared default) is an empty list.

project_doc_max_bytes.description: Combined byte budget for the whole root-to-cwd project-doc chain, processed in a single pass with a running remaining-budget counter: each file is included up to min(file_size, remaining) bytes - a file that would exceed what's left is TRUNCATED mid-content, not skipped whole, and Codex emits no warning of its own when this happens. 0 is a valid value and means Codex loads no project docs at all. Codex's own documented default is 32768 (32 KiB).

project_root_markers.description: Marker filenames used to find the project root by walking upward from the instance root (nearest ancestor containing ANY of these wins). Absent/unconfigured -> Codex's own default, ['.git']. An EXPLICITLY configured empty array is a real, valid value meaning root detection is disabled entirely (every session is treated as cwd-only, no ancestor project docs are ever read) - distinct from the key being absent. If no marker is found anywhere (even after searching to the real filesystem root), Codex also falls back to cwd-only - it never reads ancestor content 'just in case'.

hermes.description: Verified 2026-07-18 directly against the installed Hermes Agent's own Python source (git install, not a black-box wheel): agent/prompt_builder.py, agent/subdirectory_hints.py, tools/threat_patterns.py, agent/system_prompt.py. EIF has no authless way to read Hermes's own effective config.yaml live values for these specific settings (no --json mode on `hermes config show`, no dedicated introspection command) - these are the project's own asserted values, used only to compute EIF's own active-source resolution and context-budget checks. They do not change Hermes's real configuration.

parent_context_action.description: Absent by default: if a parent directory (above the instance root) already has a non-empty .hermes.md or HERMES.md, that is this instance's real active source today (Hermes's own ancestor walk, nearest match wins, no depth cap) - EIF STOPs rather than silently create a local .hermes.md that would shadow it and change effective governance for the whole subtree. Set to 'override-with-local' to explicitly authorize creating a local .hermes.md anyway. Generic adoption.mode: coexist does not imply this.

context_file_max_chars.description: Per-tier character budget for whichever context-file tier resolves as active. Hermes truncates by preserving the first 70% and last 20% of this limit (dropping the middle, with a marker noting what was cut) - not a whole-chain byte budget like Codex's. Hermes's own default is dynamically scaled to the model's context window (context_length x 4 chars/token x 0.06, floored at 20,000, ceilinged at 500,000) when a live introspection value is available; EIF has no authless way to read the live, currently-effective model context length, so its own default fallback here is the conservative 20,000-char floor, not the dynamic value - set this explicitly to match a real, larger configured Hermes limit.

knowledge.description: Where this project's knowledge artifacts live. Greenfield default is root knowledge/ + knowledge/index.md - an existing-repository adoption can point these at wherever knowledge already lives (e.g. docs/knowledge/) instead of migrating content to match EIF's default. Generated instructions, eif_generate_index.py, and eif_search_knowledge.py invocations all read these values from config - they must not hardcode 'knowledge' independently of it.

root.description: Instance-relative path to the directory eif_generate_index.py scans and eif_search_knowledge.py searches. Default on a new instance: 'knowledge'.

index_path.description: Instance-relative path to the generated index file. Default on a new instance: '<root>/index.md'. Must resolve inside knowledge.root - enforced at runtime by scripts/eif_paths.py, not just this schema (a schema pattern cannot check a resolved-path escape).

managed.description: Whether eif_init.py is allowed to generate/regenerate the knowledge index file at all. Greenfield default: true (implicit, backward-compatible). Coexist default: false - EIF must not create or overwrite a knowledge index in an adopted repository without this being explicitly turned on (--manage-knowledge-index), since the project may already have its own way of organizing knowledge that EIF should not start managing unasked. When true and an index file already exists at knowledge.index_path without EIF's ownership marker, eif_init.py still refuses to overwrite it (STOP) - this flag opts into EIF managing the index going forward, it does not itself authorize taking over an existing non-EIF file.

adoption.description: User-owned adoption/coexistence policy - deliberately NOT part of framework.lock.yaml (which is EIF-managed provenance): whether EIF coexists with pre-existing project governance is a project decision, not something EIF should infer or silently overwrite. migration_status in the lock records history (was this project greenfield or already-existing when first adopted); this section controls current behavior (how the generated block presents itself).

mode.description: greenfield: EIF-managed block may present itself as this project's baseline authority (default when eif_init finds no pre-existing entrypoint content). coexist: the generated block must not declare itself sole/primary authority, must not override pre-existing governance, and must state that project-owned instructions outside the markers stay canonical. Required to be set explicitly (via --adoption-mode) when eif_init's adoption preflight detects pre-existing entrypoint content - see scripts/eif_preflight.py.

suppressions.description: Controlled, auditable exceptions to scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py findings - independent-review redesign: FINDING-specific, not rule+path-wide. A suppression identifies one exact finding (rule + exact repo-relative path + a content fingerprint), never a whole file or a glob - a second, real finding of the same rule in the same file is NOT covered by a suppression for a different finding there, even if both happen to be on the same path. If the fingerprinted line's content changes, or the finding no longer appears at that rule+path at all, the suppression stops matching (the finding reactivates) and the scanner reports the now-dead suppression as its own 'suppression hygiene' finding - it does not just silently keep working. Never weakens a detection pattern for anyone else; see scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py for the fingerprint algorithm and the (deliberately small, hand-maintained) list of valid rule IDs - an unrecognized rule is a config error, not a silently-ignored entry.

rule.description: Stable finding category - must be one of the rule IDs scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py actually emits (e.g. 'absolute_path_leak', 'secret_shaped:password_assignment', 'secret_shaped:bearer_token', or 'denylisted_token:<N>'). An unrecognized rule ID is a hard config error, not silently ignored.

path.description: Exact repo-relative file path - glob/wildcard characters are rejected outright (broad globs are exactly what turns a reviewed one-off exception into a standing blind spot for future real findings).

fingerprint.description: 16 hex characters: the first 16 hex digits of sha256(rule + NUL + path + NUL + normalized_finding_line). Identifies the specific finding this suppression covers, not just its rule+path - a second, different finding of the same rule at the same path has a different fingerprint and is NOT suppressed by this entry. Never derived from or containing the matched secret value itself - it is a one-way hash, and the scanner's own output shows the fingerprint to copy for a finding you are reviewing, never the underlying text. Robust to the line moving within the file (line NUMBER is not part of the hash) but not to its content changing.

rationale.description: Why this specific finding is not a real issue - human-authored, reviewed text, never the matched secret value itself.

reviewed.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) this suppression was last reviewed by a human. Strictly validated - an unparseable date is a config error.

expires.description: Optional ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which this suppression no longer applies (the finding reactivates and a suppression-hygiene finding fires). Omit for no automatic expiry. Strictly validated the same as reviewed.

executable_path.description: Optional exact local executable path. It remains in the project-owned config and must never be copied into public evidence.

telemetry_enabled.description: Opt-in for EIF content-free local counters. This never enables provider telemetry or captures command content.
